implementation_notes: MRI has no inlining - each Ruby method call builds a frame, and the interpreter overhead dominates, so call elimination is worth far less than in a compiled language. The practical Ruby answers are: move the hot loop into C (a C extension), use the array gem's packed buffers to get machine-speed numeric work, or use a JIT (RubyMJIT in CRuby, which does inline hot methods but only at runtime under profile guidance). Hand-inlining a Ruby method body into a loop removes one frame per iteration and helps only for very tight loops; the readable fix is to reduce the number of method calls per iteration. Ruby 3's YJIT (the production JIT) does inline, so on Ruby 3.x the hot path is compiled and the 'no inlining' concern is largely historical - the remaining lever is shape stability (avoiding megamorphic call sites and unstable object shapes), not inlining.
idiom_name: CRuby YJIT inlines at runtime (Ruby 3.x); otherwise move hot work to a C extension or a packed buffer (array gem)
code_sketch:
# CRuby 3.x has YJIT, which does inline hot methods at runtime. On that, the
# remaining lever is shape stability, not inlining:
def step(x) = x < 0 ? 0 : x     # small: YJIT inlines it at a hot call site

# Without a JIT (or for the truly hot path), move the work out of Ruby:
require 'array'
buf = Array.new(n, 0.0)          # packed buffer: machine-speed numeric work

# A C extension is the real 'inline everything' for MRI:
#   def sum(xs); ...; end   compiled as C, the interpreter never runs
pitfalls: MRI historically had no inlining at all; on Ruby 3.x YJIT inlines at runtime, so hand-inlining a method body into a loop is usually obsolete.
Hand-inlining a Ruby method to remove a frame duplicates the logic and only helps very tight loops; the bigger win is fewer calls per iteration or a C extension.
Shape instability (objects with differing shapes at one call site) defeats YJIT's inline caches the same way it does in JavaScript.
An Array of Floats boxes each element in MRI; the array gem's packed buffer is the machine-speed equivalent and is what makes numeric work fast.
alternative: CRuby 3.x with YJIT enabled, or move the hot work into a C extension / the array gem's packed buffers rather than hand-inlining
